text:
ops-bot: Alert: SLO breach detected - streaming.p95 > 800ms in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Automatic incident created.

sam: I'm seeing p95 spike to ~1s and p99 near 2.6s for streaming-chat endpoints. Traces show long waits before first token.

priya: can we correlate with deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy event: "prefix-hash-rewrite" promoted to global at 1812395400 by infra-sre.

rachel: oh. That was the keyspace change that touched prefix-cache keys.

infra-sre: confirming: we rolled the prefix hashing logic to v3. We also updated the cache key format.

sam: dashboards show prefix-cache effective hit rate dropping from 85% -> 4% starting at 1812396000. Throughput stayed similar but tail latency ballooned.

priya: streaming stalls consistent with cache-miss shock: each miss triggers full model initialization + disk read in some clusters. That explains p99.

infra-sre: paging note: some worker pods started heavy paging due to more IO on model shards when cache cold. Memory pressure increased on nodes with mixed workloads.

ops-bot: paging alert: node-pressure-high on model-shard nodes (cluster-a).

sam: immediate mitigations: 1) rollback prefix-hash to previous format; 2) add temporary aliasing layer so v3 checks v2 keys; 3) temporarily divert traffic to dedicated capacity (if we have warm pools). Thoughts?

rachel: dedicated pools are available but take a few minutes to switch. Aliasing might be safest if we can implement fast key lookup fallback in the edge.

infra-sre: we can flip traffic back to v2 quickly. Aliasing requires code path change and may risk more complexity under load. Recommend rollback first, then follow up with alias/backfill.

priya: agree. If rollback goes smooth, do background warmup to repopulate cache.

sam: ok infra-sre, execute rollback and post the curl command when done. I'll set an abort window and monitor p95/p99 and node paging.

infra-sre: starting rollback now: ``POST /deploys/rollback prefix-hash-rewrite -> v2``

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by infra-sre at 1812400120.

observability-bot: alert: set temporary watch - notify channel if streaming.p95 > 500ms for more than 2 consecutive minutes.

rachel: logs show errors like: ``WARN prefix_cache.get miss key=ph3:7f2b -> falling back to model read (latency=1230ms)`` repeated.

cs: two customers have reported sessions timing out. Escalating to their on-call.

infra-sre: rollback completed at 1812400255. Traffic restored to v2.

sam: metrics: p95 fell to ~150ms within 90s after rollback. p99 now ~430ms. Prefix-cache hit rate back to ~80% after warmup.

priya: paging alerts cleared on cluster-a. Memory reclaimed.

rachel: good. For the post-rollback period I'm sampling traces to confirm streaming token throughput is back to normal. Early samples look clean.

ops-bot: Incident severity changed to "mitigated". Post-incident follow-up required.

sam: action items: - postmortem documenting cause (prefix key format change without backfill/alias) - add deploy gating: require per-region cache-hit sanity checks for 15m at canary before global promotion - implement automatic rollback trigger when prefix-cache hit delta > 40% within 10m - create backfill/alias helper in cache service to populate ph_v3 from ph_v2 on rollout - run a canary test in CI that simulates hash-change and validates no mass cache miss.

infra-sre: I'll file the rollback runbook improvements and add a console button for emergency revert.

priya: I'll add streaming-specific SLO submetrics: streaming-first-token latency and stall-count per minute.

cs: I'll send a ready-to-send customer note: short explanation + mitigation + timeline, once postmortem draft is available.

rachel: scheduling a 60-min blameless postmortem tomorrow. I'll attach timeline graphs and traces.

sam: handoff: I'm going to rest. priya, can you be primary for the 1-hour monitoring window?

priya: ack. I'll watch p99 and node pages.

ops-bot: Handoff: sam -> priya in 5m.

priya: thanks everyone. Closing active incident thread but keeping channel open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
